prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, half-length demi statue portrait — a sculpted figure ending at the waist. ONE woman, angled 45 degrees toward the camera, framed so her whole sculpted form is visible from the top of her head down to one single, deliberately carved rounded base at her waist, her face in natural scale with her body — never an oversized close-up crop of just the face. Where her sculpted form comes to an end at her waist, it is because the sculpture itself ends there, not because a camera frame happens to cut her off.

Subject: A real photograph of a strikingly beautiful adult Chinese woman in weixun makeup — clear fair skin, a warm rose-red wash blended across the outer corners of both eyes and drifting up toward the temples, the same flush spreading softly across the cheekbones and the bridge of the nose, slightly smudged, dewy highlights, soft brown-pink eyeshadow, large moist eyes with bright real catchlights and a faint glassy shine, moist rose-tinted lips, long black hair loosely tousled with a few strands across the face, a dreamy, half-lidded expression. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain, real living eyes with bright catchlights and genuine depth, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real face, not an illustration, not a render, not cel-shaded. On each ear a big rose-gold hoop hangs clear of the neck down to the shoulder.

Physique: A colossal heavy chest, a still-visible cinched waist, a big soft rounded belly below the waistline hanging heavily, very thick soft arms.

Body: From the collarbones down, her whole body — both shoulders, both arms and hands, her chest and belly — is not painted, covered or clothed but physically carved from ONE solid block of genuine turquoise, a vivid sky-blue to blue-green stone laced with fine dark matrix veining running through it in irregular webs, polished to a smooth, cool sheen, completely opaque. It is one continuous sculpted mass, never hollow, with no seam and no skin anywhere, every wrist, palm, finger and knuckle the same stone. At her waist, the whole solid form curves inward evenly on every side and rounds off into one single, smooth, polished base — the stone simply reaching its natural end there, the one rounded base resting flat on the surface beneath her.

Opacity: everything below the collarbones is solid, completely opaque turquoise — no light passes through it at any point. It has the same cool, hard, dense solidity throughout, catching light only as bright highlights on its polished surface, never glowing from within. Her face, by contrast, is warm, soft, living flesh, its natural colour nowhere close to the colour of the stone.

Boundary: a sharp jagged line runs around the base of the neck and across both collarbones — real skin above, material immediately below. There is no line down the centre of her body. At that line, the stone's edge rises in a small raised step above her flesh, casting a crisp shadow — her skin beside it stays smooth and even. The rounded base at her waist is the material's own carved finish, always the clean, deliberate result of a sculpture — never the edge of a photograph. Shards interlock along the collarbone line only.

Setting: a huge backdrop behind her washed with two coloured lights from behind — a soft sky blue on one side and a pale sandy beige on the other, blending into a smooth gradient in the middle, and a glossy dark floor beneath her.

Pose: her left hand (solid material) resting at her waist, her right hand (solid material) held at chest height clear of her body, both hands well away from her face, head tilted slightly toward the camera.

Lighting: two large softboxes rake across her body from either side, so sky-blue light glances off the left half and sandy-beige light glances off the right half, catching in bright reflections. A soft frontal light falls on her face and ears only. Only her face, ears and neck read as real skin. shot on a Hasselblad X2D with an 85mm lens, shallow depth of field. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
